notes: The DECP API works without a login, but the dataset is of no use for this thesis. It has 15 records mentioning NGS, sequencing or Illumina, and none is later than 2023. The relevant ones are small hospital contracts from 2019–2023, mostly worth €0.1–0.5M. Vendor names are mostly null (only SIRET ids), and buyer names are mostly null too (ids only). It has no records for INSERM, CNRS, Institut Pasteur or CNRGH sequencing awards. Large research purchases are not in this dataset, probably because they are published as TED/BOAMP notices or awarded under a no-competition exemption. The one lead is TED notice 640137-2023, an INSERM Paris contract for Illumina reagents for the Cochin and SFR Necker genomics platforms. It carries an estimated value of €8M excl. VAT and was awarded without competition under Art. R.2122-3 because the reagents are Illumina-only. That is a search-result snippet; I could not open the notice PDF. The notice shows that French research buyers are locked in by technical exclusivity, and it gives no price trend. It does not support or contradict the thesis. The snippet gives no award date (only 2023), no winner, no duration and no outcome, so it is not enough for an evidence item.
how_to_mine: Skip DECP. Instead use the TED search (ted.europa.eu) or the BOAMP search for 'Illumina' or 'NovaSeq' with CPV 38000000/33696500, restricted to the buyers INSERM, CNRS, CEA/CNRGH, Institut Pasteur and Institut Curie. Look for award notices with value and duration, and for any 2025–26 notices that name Element, Ultima, MGI or Roche. The aim is to compare Illumina framework values over time and to find non-Illumina awardees. Also try marchesonline.com award pages (AO-9635473, a 2026 Resah NGS framework, max €5M, which may name awardees).
new_candidates: TED notice 640137-2023 (INSERM Paris, Illumina reagents, €8M est., exclusivity justification) - https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/640137-2023/pdf
